sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *antes de que* and *después de que* from B2 Unit 7. *Antes de que* always takes the subjunctive: after a past verb, the imperfect subjunctive (*antes de que llegaran*). *Después de que* takes the indicative for something that happened (*después de que llegaron*) and the subjunctive for something still to come. The two are ideal for putting the events of a single day in order.

sections.title: Ordering the events of the day
rows: Allende habló por radio antes de que los aviones bombardearan el palacio.
Allende spoke on the radio before the planes bombed the palace. (*antes de que* + imperfect subjunctive)
Después de que los aviones bombardearon el palacio, los soldados entraron.
After the planes bombed the palace, the soldiers went in. (*después de que* + indicative: it happened)
Antes de que terminara la dictadura, muchas familias buscaban a sus desaparecidos.
Before the dictatorship ended, many families were looking for their disappeared. (*antes de que* + subjunctive)
Después de que terminó la dictadura, se publicaron informes sobre las víctimas.
After the dictatorship ended, reports about the victims were published. (indicative)

items.spanish: Antes de que llegara la noche, el centro de Santiago estaba vacío.
items.english: Before night came, the centre of Santiago was empty.

items.spanish: Después de que terminó el golpe, empezó la dictadura.
items.english: After the coup ended, the dictatorship began.

items.spanish: Hablamos del museo antes de que lo visitáramos.
items.english: We talked about the museum before we visited it.

sections.content: Two questions decide the verb. After *antes de que*: always the subjunctive, so *antes de que llegara*, never *antes de que llegó*. After *después de que*: has it happened? Yes: indicative (*después de que llegó*). Not yet: subjunctive.
